title: Matrix Rust SDK replacement owned security and delivery risk register

status_definitions.open: The risk requires technical work, evidence, or a decision.
status_definitions.mitigating: Controls have landed, but continuing exposure or gate evidence remains.
status_definitions.blocked_on_decision: Implementation is stopped pending an owned decision.
status_definitions.accepted: An authorized reviewer explicitly accepted the residual for a bounded period.
status_definitions.closed: Closure criteria are met and linked evidence has been reviewed.
status_definitions.superseded: A replacement risk record owns the remaining exposure.

governance_rules: R0.2 documents and assigns technical risks but does not close them.

Critical and high technical risks remain unresolved with status open, mitigating, or blocked_on_decision; they may not become accepted, closed, or superseded without independently reviewed closure evidence and documented authority.
Accepted status requires accepted_by, accepted_at, rationale, and acceptance_expires_at.
A dated review finding disposition is distinct from the ongoing systemic risk status.
Evidence must identify the reviewed immutable commit and green non-cancelled CI where applicable.

risks.title: Rust 1.93 and cross-platform release-toolchain compatibility
risks.closure_criteria: Immutable macOS and Linux build/package evidence proves Rust 1.93, Tauri 2, exact SDK dependencies, signing/notarization assumptions, runners, and caches, with no unowned residual.
evidence_targets: green platform CI on reviewed SHA

risks.title: matrix-sdk-ui and widget API stability
risks.closure_criteria: Exact pins and compile/live probes cover every enabled experimental API, with explicit approval and an upgrade/exit policy.

risks.title: Element Call and MatrixRTC parity
risks.closure_criteria: Current call behavior passes packaged macOS/Linux parity, CSP/origin review, cleanup tests, and contains no hidden JS SDK exception.

risks.title: Legacy JS IndexedDB crypto store and device identity cannot be reused safely
risks.closure_criteria: Migration uses reauthentication and a new device, exercises recovery, and never guesses or silently copies a legacy token/device ID.

risks.title: Large matrix-js-sdk product dependency surface
risks.closure_criteria: AST inventory reaches zero product imports and no JS-owned Matrix runtime, type, store, token, media, service-worker, call, or widget path remains.

risks.title: IPC ordering and backpressure corrupt client state
risks.closure_criteria: Frozen cross-language contract proves checked sequencing, stale-generation rejection, bounded queues, deterministic resync, and producer cancellation under property/fault tests.

risks.title: Concurrent Matrix client owners or production backend selector
risks.closure_criteria: Runtime and process tests prove one Rust supervisor owner, no shared device/session identity, no selector, and complete JS client shutdown before Rust activation.

risks.title: Custom agent events lose required raw content
risks.closure_criteria: Bounded Synara-owned raw content preserves required semantics and passes shared hostile/golden fixtures without SDK objects or arbitrary unbounded JSON crossing IPC.

risks.title: UIA and registration API gaps encourage unsafe fallback
risks.closure_criteria: Exact SDK APIs or an approved upstream change cover UIA/registration with live tests; no raw Matrix REST fallback exists.

risks.title: Search semantics diverge from current product behavior
risks.closure_criteria: Server/local strategy, filters, pagination, cancellation, and stale-result behavior pass owned parity cases.

risks.title: Media transport leaks data or exhausts memory
risks.closure_criteria: Authenticated native retrieval/decryption uses bounded cache or local handles, validates metadata, revokes access, and sends no media bytes through JSON IPC.

risks.title: Store keys, session secrets, or sensitive diagnostics leak
risks.closure_criteria: Production native vault, secret-aware types, producer-side allowlists, hostile fixtures, and scans prove prohibited secrets/content never reach files, IPC, UI errors, logs, or support exports.

risks.title: Long-lived integration branch diverges from main
risks.closure_criteria: Each reconciliation is reviewed for semantic conflicts and the full affected gate is rerun; final closure occurs when the integration branch merges or is retired.

risks.title: Implementation agent strays or masks failures
risks.closure_criteria: Every task uses the reviewed native-agent packet/template, bounded files, explicit stop conditions, independent diff review, correction loop, and reproduced validation.

risks.title: CI cancellation or branch policy permits unvalidated merges
risks.closure_criteria: Workflow policy and repository required-check configuration prevent cancelled/stale runs from authorizing merge, and every accepted PR cites a green non-cancelled run on the reviewed SHA.
evidence_targets: verified integration-branch protection after PR #77: Quality gate and Desktop package gate required, strict/up-to-date checks, administrator enforcement, conversation resolution, and force-push/delete disabled

risks.title: Store deletion races a live client or task
risks.closure_criteria: Order-sensitive tests prove reject work, cancel/join, close client/store, clear credentials/key, then exact wipe; all injected failures have deterministic retry states.

risks.title: Store paths escape through traversal, symlinks, or races
risks.closure_criteria: Absolute canonical confinement and component no-follow semantics survive malicious pre-existing roots, child symlinks, replacement races, traversal, and exact-delete tests.

risks.title: IPC integer, stream identity, and payload ambiguity
risks.closure_criteria: Rust and TypeScript reject the same maximum/overflow/unsafe-integer/stream-mismatch/unbounded/secret-like/media-byte corpus and the v1 contract is frozen.

risks.title: Migration scaffolding or JS compatibility becomes permanent
risks.closure_criteria: Zero-use inventory and deletion review prove all JS SDK, selector, service-worker auth, bridge, legacy cleanup, and migration-only code is removed or has an approved time-bounded deletion gate.

risks.title: FNV-1a account directory identity can collide
risks.closure_criteria: A versioned normalized identity derivation uses a collision-resistant digest with documented migration before real stores exist and adversarial collision/isolation tests pass.

risks.title: Declared store layout does not match SDK-owned directories
risks.closure_criteria: Documented state/crypto/cache/media ownership matches exact SDK 0.18 builder behavior and live encrypted open/reopen evidence on both platforms.

risks.title: Existing encrypted store plus missing key can create a replacement key
risks.closure_criteria: Existing-store key miss returns a recoverable locked/corrupt state, preserves data, never generates a replacement, and passes failure/retry tests.

risks.title: SDK store passphrase copies persist outside secret-aware memory
risks.closure_criteria: The exact SDK API boundary and unavoidable copies are documented, secret-aware wrappers and zeroization are used where supported, and Debug/log/IPC tests prove no material escapes.

risks.title: Legacy WebView fallback and service worker retain Matrix credentials, while platform persistence durability varies until cutover
risks.current_manifestation: At integration SHA 2aa6d96f9b63aad64a14feac23df2f694857be85, createLocalStorageSessionStore deliberately writes the access token, device ID, user ID, base URL, and session generation to WebView localStorage when native session persistence is unavailable. Platform status separately documents session-scoped stores that may not survive restart and Windows builds without native session persistence. Secure native restore, weaker WebView fallback, and platform durability are therefore distinct behaviors. The fallback makes credentials available to the WebView context and is weaker under XSS; this behavior predates the Rust replacement and is not newly introduced by Rust, and no observed credential disclosure is asserted.
risks.closure_criteria: After cutover, Rust owns all Matrix session material and service-worker auth and credential-bearing WebView localStorage are deleted. Secure native restore is specified and tested separately from fallback and platform durability: every supported platform either restores from an approved durable native store or fails explicitly into the approved reauthentication/recovery state, never silently stores a token in the WebView; unsupported Windows persistence is explicit. Packaged tests cover clean quit/relaunch, crash/relaunch, OS restart, and native-store unavailable/locked cases, and scans/runtime tests prove no credential remains in WebView/service-worker storage or crosses IPC.
evidence_targets: post-cutover sessions.ts and service-worker secret scan proving no credential-bearing localStorage fallback
platform/secrets.ts persistence matrix distinguishing durable native restore, session-scoped/unavailable recovery, and unsupported Windows persistence
packaged macOS/Linux clean-quit, crash, OS-restart, and native-store unavailable/locked restore-or-reauthentication tests plus explicit Windows unsupported-state test

risks.title: Legacy cleanup, retention, and cutover marker are incomplete or over-broad
risks.closure_criteria: Retention and marker policies are approved; cleanup targets only exact Matrix legacy keys/stores, preserves unrelated data, is idempotent, requires correct confirmation, and passes interruption tests.

risks.title: Raw SDK errors, URLs, identifiers, and absolute paths reach diagnostics
risks.closure_criteria: All producers emit stable allowlisted categories and hostile tests prove no full identifier, URL, absolute path, raw SDK string, secret, or content appears in any diagnostic surface.

risks.title: Wipe and credential deletion are not failure-atomic
risks.current_manifestation: At integration SHA 2aa6d96f9b63aad64a14feac23df2f694857be85, clearPersistedSessions catches native credential-store removal and Matrix IndexedDB deletion failures, records a completed diagnostic, and returns success; performLogout then continues clearing other state and reloads. A failed logout or wipe can therefore leave credential or Matrix store data behind without a user-visible recoverable failure while the UI behaves as though cleanup completed. This is a false-completion and retained-state risk; it is not evidence that disclosure has occurred.
risks.closure_criteria: Every filesystem, keyring, and session-state deletion is verified and fail-closed. Native credential-store or Matrix IndexedDB deletion failure produces a specified user-visible recoverable state and retry/support path, emits no completed result, causes no false completion or reload, preserves enough state for a safe idempotent retry, and never triggers automatic wipe. Injected failures for each deletion independently and together prove the behavior, and success is reported only after both removals are verified.
evidence_targets: R0.5 failure matrix covering native credential-store and Matrix IndexedDB deletion independently and together
sessionPersistence.ts injected-failure tests proving verified deletion, fail-closed completion, and idempotent retry
initMatrix.ts logout and clear-login tests proving a visible recoverable failure and no reload on deletion failure

risks.title: Matrix Rust store/session vault lacks production OS credential-store integration
risks.closure_criteria: Scoped macOS Keychain and Linux Secret Service adapters persist and reopen Matrix store/session material, fail explicitly when unavailable, and contain no production in-memory/file/WebView fallback.

risks.title: Native media security and lifecycle, including Blob URL reclamation, are unspecified
risks.current_manifestation: Current Matrix media consumers create Blob URLs without reclaiming them. ThumbnailContent and ImageContent do so only for encrypted media; their clear-media paths use resolved HTTP URLs. VideoContent, AudioContent, PDF/file rendering and fallback download, and FileHeader fallback download create Blob URLs for both clear and encrypted media. Local image/video upload-metadata extraction also creates Blob URLs independently of the eventual room encryption state. The existing useObjectURL cleanup hook is not used by these producers. Unreclaimed URLs retain resources and can extend decrypted-Blob lifetime. This observation does not establish disk or network disclosure.
risks.closure_criteria: Instrument Blob URL creation and revocation and prove exactly-once release for every actual producer: encrypted ThumbnailContent and ImageContent; clear and encrypted VideoContent, AudioContent, PDF/file rendering, fallback file download, and FileHeader fallback download; and local image/video upload-metadata previews. Exercise replacement, retry, failure, viewer close, unmount, cancellation, and completed fallback-save terminal conditions; document or process exit does not count as cleanup. Clear ThumbnailContent/ImageContent resolved HTTP URLs are not Blob URL producers but remain subject to URL/authentication lifecycle policy. The threat-reviewed native pipeline also validates URL, size, content/MIME, filename/disposition, and encrypted metadata; bounds cache/temp persistence; prevents unintended decrypted persistence; and passes malicious-content and lifecycle tests.
evidence_targets: instrumented tests proving encrypted-only Blob URL creation/reclamation for ThumbnailContent and ImageContent while clear paths remain resolved HTTP URLs

instrumented tests proving clear/encrypted Blob URL creation and exactly-once reclamation for VideoContent, AudioContent, FileContent PDF/file rendering and fallback save, and FileHeader fallback save
msgContent local image/video upload-metadata tests proving reclamation independently of eventual room encryption
media design and hostile integration suite

risks.title: Widget and call origins/CSP, experimental features, or incomplete teardown expand trust and state lifetime
risks.current_manifestation: At integration SHA 2aa6d96f9b63aad64a14feac23df2f694857be85, CallEmbed.start registers four Matrix listeners with freshly allocated this.method.bind(this) callbacks, while dispose attempts to remove them with different freshly allocated bound callbacks. Because listener removal is identity-based, dispose does not detach those registrations, potentially retaining disposed call/widget state and processing later Matrix events. This establishes a teardown and post-dispose-processing defect, not a proven credential or content disclosure.
risks.closure_criteria: Every Matrix listener uses a stable callback or stored disposer identity, and call/widget teardown is exact and idempotent. Tests prove listener counts return to baseline and no event is delivered after disposal across hangup or replacement, the approved room-navigation lifecycle, logout, and window close. Explicit origin allowlists, least-privilege CSP, capability scope, secret handling, and experimental-feature acceptance must still pass packaged security tests.
evidence_targets: CallEmbed lifecycle tests asserting baseline listener counts and no post-dispose delivery across hangup/replacement, room navigation, logout, and window close
Phase 10 origin, CSP, capability, secret-handling, experimental-feature, and packaged acceptance evidence

risks.title: Crash, incomplete migration, downgrade, and rollback behavior can reopen or destroy incompatible state
risks.closure_criteria: Incomplete-store, crash, prior-build rollback, and downgrade policies are approved and tested with inert legacy data, no concurrent clients, no auto-wipe, and bounded retention.

risks.title: Over-broad Tauri Matrix commands or capabilities expose privileged operations
risks.closure_criteria: Only purpose-specific bounded commands are registered, capabilities are least privilege, and unauthorized/malformed invocation tests pass.

risks.title: Proxy URLs can contain credentials, unsafe schemes, or diagnostic data
risks.owner_role: Network configuration and diagnostic privacy owners
risks.closure_criteria: A parsed scheme/host policy rejects embedded credentials by default, avoids broad allowlists, and all errors/diagnostics use redacted categories.

risks.title: Mandatory governance and live-evidence gates were bypassed
risks.closure_criteria: Every Section 17 artifact is reviewed, P0.5/P0.6 residuals are evidenced or explicitly scoped, live Phase 2/P3.1 evidence passes, and formal truthful reports close only supported gates.

risks.title: Personal identifiers and paths are inconsistently classified as non-secret
risks.closure_criteria: Data classification treats full user/device IDs, homeserver/proxy URLs, and absolute paths as personal-sensitive and diagnostics contain none unless an explicit reviewed exception exists.
evidence_targets: R0.6 classification contract and hostile fixtures

risks.title: Forwarding accepts undecrypted or decryption-failure encrypted events
risks.current_manifestation: The current forwarding helper reads MatrixEvent.getContent() and spreads returned fields into a new m.room.message without first requiring successful clear content and an approved clear event type. Raw, in-progress, or otherwise unprocessed m.room.encrypted events can therefore republish wire algorithm, ciphertext, sender_key, device_id, and session_id fields; completed decryption failures can forward m.bad.encrypted diagnostic placeholder content. Successfully decrypted events forward clear content. This is a forwarding correctness and metadata-privacy/correlation risk, not evidence of plaintext disclosure, Megolm key disclosure, or unintended encrypted-attachment key disclosure.
risks.closure_criteria: Forwarding rejects m.room.encrypted events without successfully decrypted clear content, rejects m.bad.encrypted and other decryption-failure placeholders, allowlists approved clear event types and fields, and fails closed for mixed or multi-select batches. Tests cover successful, raw/in-progress, and failed decryption into encrypted and unencrypted target rooms and prove wire algorithm, ciphertext, sender_key, device_id, and session_id fields are never republished. Standards-required encrypted-attachment file descriptors from successfully decrypted clear content remain preserved, subject to the existing unencrypted-target confirmation; closure does not require attachment re-upload/re-encryption and does not assert a plaintext, Megolm-key, or unintended attachment-key leak.
evidence_targets: synara/src/app/utils/__tests__/forward.test.ts cases for successful, raw/in-progress, and failed decryption; field allowlisting; encrypted-attachment descriptors; and mixed-batch fail-closed behavior
Message.tsx and RoomTimeline.tsx single/batch integration tests for encrypted and unencrypted target rooms
P13.5 evidence that algorithm, ciphertext, sender_key, device_id, and session_id wire fields are not republished

risks.title: Authentication callback tokens remain in URL state without a complete integrity policy
risks.current_manifestation: At integration SHA 2aa6d96f9b63aad64a14feac23df2f694857be85, Login.tsx reads loginToken from the browser URL, rewrites it into the login URL for hash-router handling, and passes it to TokenLogin, with no URL/history scrub in that flow. This extends token lifetime in URL/history-visible state and leaves strict callback-origin, replay, malformed-token, and target OAuth state/nonce/PKCE integrity policy unspecified. This is a token-lifetime/exposure and callback-integrity risk, not evidence of observed account compromise.
risks.closure_criteria: Consume each login token once and scrub it from URL and history before any asynchronous work or UI rendering. The token never persists in referrer-visible state, browser history, logs, diagnostics, or storage; callback origin is strictly validated; replay and malformed callbacks fail closed. The target OAuth/OIDC callback validates state, nonce, and PKCE according to the selected flow. Hash-router and history-router tests plus hostile callback fixtures prove one-time consumption, immediate scrub, strict origin, integrity validation, and safe error handling.
evidence_targets: Login.tsx callback handler review proving consume-once and pre-render/pre-async URL/history scrub
hash-router and history-router authentication callback tests
hostile origin, replay, malformed token, state, nonce, and PKCE callback fixtures
P13.5 URL, history, referrer, log, diagnostic, and storage token-negative evidence

risks.title: OS notification privacy metadata and approval-content redaction are not enforced end to end
risks.current_manifestation: At integration SHA 2aa6d96f9b63aad64a14feac23df2f694857be85, showPlatformNotification normalizes a notification privacy field but omits it when constructing the desktop notification request. Agent approval notifications can also append commandPreview to the OS-visible body. The OS boundary can therefore lose the caller's privacy intent and receive sensitive approval command text. This is a notification privacy-policy and data-minimization defect, not evidence of observed disclosure.
risks.closure_criteria: Preserve a validated privacy field end to end across the notification DTO, IPC command, native adapter, and OS presentation. An approved policy redacts title/body/action context for encrypted rooms, private mode, and lock-screen presentation; sensitive approval command previews never enter OS notifications. Packaged platform tests and negative IPC/OS-notification fixtures prove privacy-field preservation, redaction behavior, bounded metadata, and absence of command-preview or event-content leakage.
evidence_targets: platform/notifications.ts and native desktop notification adapter tests proving end-to-end privacy-field preservation
ClientNonUIFeatures.tsx approval notification tests proving commandPreview never reaches an OS notification
packaged macOS/Linux encrypted-room, private-mode, and lock-screen redaction tests
negative IPC and OS-notification fixtures for approval commands and sensitive event content

review_finding_dispositions.note: Documentation does not repair destructive ordering or partial failure.
Canonical and symlink-safe confinement remains unimplemented.
Raw diagnostic data and privacy classification remain technical defects.
Cross-language safe counters and checked overflow remain unimplemented.
Authoritative stream identity and typed bounded bodies remain unimplemented.
Exact SDK directory ownership and live reopen proof remain outstanding.
Collision-resistant versioned account identity remains unimplemented.

evidence: independent post-PR-#77 integration-branch protection verification: Quality gate and Desktop package gate required; strict/up-to-date checks; administrators enforced; conversation resolution required; force pushes and deletion disabled
review_finding_dispositions.note: The dated finding is accepted as remediated by the reviewed R0.1 PRs, exact-SHA green evidence, and independent verification of the current integration-branch protection and required-check configuration after PR #77. The systemic risks remain mitigating because repository settings can drift and every future merge still requires a green non-cancelled run on the reviewed SHA.
R0.2 can create governance artifacts, but live evidence and formal gate acceptance remain R0.7/R0.8 work.
